why: The pulse attributes to BTIG's Krinsky a historical stat ('eight prior episodes... seven lost about 10% over 30 days') that does not appear in the source note and inverts its actual finding, which the note itself calls 'a coin-toss' with a slightly positive 20-day average return (+0.31%, 53% higher) — a mechanism the note does not argue, even though the correctly-cited 73% figure and the mechanical vol-crush/dealer-hedging chain from the Nomura McElligott note elsewhere in the same theme are preserved accurately.
